scores.notes: Fidelity 9, surreal 8, heat/aesthetic 8, rules 9, producibility 9. Best placement: it is the only design whose clock runs forward (sunset, then first star, then night, then 15's storm night), and the empty sofa after Mila's exit is the strongest image here. Its 'morning light across Kira's eyes' is the best reading of her own line 'Knows how it smells in the morning' and obeys #081. Writes Kira's hair as 'true black, never blue' (avoids the known navy-hair trap) and costs the shots from NOW.md. Weak points: the wet sleeve (M4) is too literal; the canvas-rectangle shadow (M1) is less grounded than the sculpture shadow her own 'legs like Giacometti sculptures' gives. Taken into the final: M2 morning light, M5 empty sofa with Mila only in the reflection, M3 craquelure, the bell under it, the placement.

Fidelity 8, surreal 9, heat/aesthetic 9, rules 8, producibility 8. The richest heat in gesture: the wrist grip shedding pastel dust (her 'collectors touch their Degas'), the reflection that keeps posing (her 'muscle memory of poses'), and an oil-paint stroke hanging in the air (her 'air thickens like oil paint'). Losses: L5 moves #085's sand moment indoors and drops the sand; L2 invents a male-on-male charge between Ule and Jean-Marc and puts 'Sotheby's' on screen; its prompts say 'wavy blue-black hair' (renders navy); L5 uses Mila as the first reference without saying so. Taken into the final: Kira's out-of-focus shoulder in the foreground, the camera standing where Kira stands, the near-still motion discipline, and the craquelure guard ('not wrinkles, not wounds'). The pastel dust and posing reflection are offered as alternates.

Fidelity 8, surreal 10, heat/aesthetic 7, rules 8, producibility 7. The strongest single surreal ideas: the sculpture shadow, the blank auction lot tag on the scratched bangle, and above all the ultramarine pigment that falls off her dress instead of sand ('too expensive, too pure, undiluted by turpentine'). Problems: M1 needs four faces in one frame; M2 stacks four text lines into 6 s; its order runs sunset, then night, then 'first star', which goes backwards in time; its bridge card writes new text onto never-cut shot 15; 'wavy blue-black hair' is the navy trap. Taken into the final: the sculpture shadow (M1) and the falling ultramarine pigment (M4). The lot tag is offered as the alternate for M1.

cast.mila: Photorealistic waist-up reference portrait, 16:9, soft neutral daylight, plain warm-grey studio wall, 35mm film grain, real skin pores, no retouching. An original, non-famous young woman, a high-fashion campaign model: very tall and very slender, a long thin neck, narrow shoulders, fine collarbones. Very pale skin, as if it has never known sun. Eyes the colour of faded blue denim, beautiful and empty: the practised gaze of a model on the thirtieth take, the pose held from muscle memory. A calm, composed face like a mask held slightly too tight; a faint smile that has a price. Pale ash-blonde hair scraped back smooth and tight. Thin long fingers with a nude manicure resting at her collarbone; on that wrist a slim flat gold bangle dulled by fine scratches. A black body-contoured knit dress with bare shoulders that clings like a second skin. No text, no logos.
cast.jean_marc: Photorealistic waist-up reference portrait, 16:9, soft neutral daylight, plain warm-grey studio wall, 35mm film grain, real skin pores, no retouching. An original, non-famous French man around fifty, a very wealthy art collector: handsome in a polished, practised way, dark hair silvering at the temples and swept back, clean-shaven, an even light tan. A smile rehearsed for cameras at an art fair: perfect, a fraction too exact, never reaching his eyes. Cool appraiser's eyes that study the viewer the way an expert verifies a canvas. Under the polish, a faint strain around the eyes: a man who owes. An immaculate pale stone-grey summer suit, open-collar white shirt, no tie; the jacket falls open on a pale silk lining. Manicured hands held with a proprietor's stillness. No text, no logos.

shots.prompt: 16:9 cinematic film still, total photographic realism, 35mm film grain, real skin texture, luxury underground arthouse, not glossy. Late afternoon on a weathered wooden jetty in a black-sand volcanic bay, a dark storm front low on the horizon, the water the colour of molten copper under a low sun. A small white seaplane rocks on its floats at the end of the jetty. The tall young woman from the second reference image has just stepped from the float onto the planks: extremely long, thin bare legs, a black body-contoured knit dress pressed to her by the wind like a second skin, empty eyes. The man from the third reference image, pale stone-grey summer suit, holds her waist with one flat, possessive palm and looks ahead, not at her. Left foreground, out of focus: the back of the head and one bare shoulder of the woman from the first reference image, glossy jet-black wavy hair (true black, never blue), standing slightly behind, watching. The low sun throws long shadows along the planks. One impossible detail, treated as ordinary: the model's shadow is not a woman's shadow but the shadow of a thread-thin, rough-surfaced bronze sculpture of a walking figure; every other shadow is normal. No text, no logos.

Background left, soft focus but readable, a small white seaplane behind them: the tall young woman from the second reference image in a black body-contoured knit dress, and the man from the third reference image closing his fingers lightly around her thin wrist, just above a scratched gold bangle: an owner's grip. shots.title: Cracks by the eyes
shots.line: Silent text: "M. — mask too tight, cracks by the eyes." (#085) · Sound, no text: the valley church bell strikes three times ("Somewhere below, in the valley, the Catholic church bell struck three times", #085)
shots.prompt: 16:9 cinematic close-up, total photographic realism, real skin pores, 35mm film grain. An open-air restaurant above black volcanic sand in the last minutes of sunset; behind, out of focus, the sea the colour of molten copper; frangipani blossoms on a white cloth. Close profile of the young woman from the first reference image, face exactly as in the reference, pale ash-blonde hair scraped back, eyes the colour of faded denim lowered toward the sea, a detached, stolen silence; a white silk-and-lace dress with thin straps, bare shoulder and collarbone lit copper, lips slightly parted. One impossible detail, photographed with total realism and treated as normal: at the outer corners of her eyes, and only there, the skin carries fine craquelure, the hairline crack network in the varnish of a centuries-old oil portrait, dry and faintly golden; not wrinkles, not wounds, no blood, no peeling. The rest of her skin is flawless, too perfect. Across the table, soft focus, the man from the second reference image studies her profile from close without touching her, with the cold attention of an expert examining a forgery. Nobody reacts. Luxury, adult, unsettling. No text, no logos, no glasses, no bottles.

interpretations_for_elena:
Nothing below is literally in your text. Each one is yours to keep, change or drop.

1. WHO IS 'I'. In #082 the narrator is a woman ('Я узнала'), and she is a different person from Kira: 'I' shakes Mila's hand while 'Kira stands slightly behind, watching.' The film has no narrator character, so I gave that narrator's gaze to Kira's position: the camera stands behind her in M1, and her shoulder is in frame in M5. No first-person line goes on screen. 'I watch her bare feet' (#083) is used only as an image.

2. KIRA AND MILA: MY READING, NOT CANON. Your text gives recognition, not desire:
- 'Knows this pain by name. / Knows how it smells in the morning.' (#082)
- 'I watch her bare feet' (#083)
- 'Mila leans toward me, asks about dessert.' (#084)
Because Kira is a lesbian (#053), I read a possible quiet charge in that watching. I staged it as gaze only (M2, M5): no touch, no exchanged look of desire. As shot, it plays as recognition. You can warm it, or keep it cool.

3. 'HOW IT SMELLS IN THE MORNING'. I read this as Kira's own sobriety and recovery. The links are #086 ('Kira tried to avoid alcohol… graduated from that school, the memory carved deep of when she disgusted herself') and #085 ('every morning you rebuild yourself from yesterday's wreckage'). M2's dawn light rests on that reading.

4. EVERY SURREAL DETAIL IS MY TRANSLATION OF ONE OF YOUR LINES:
- M1 sculpture shadow ← 'legs like Giacometti sculptures' + 'another lot'
- M2 dawn light ← 'how it smells in the morning'
- M3 craquelure ← 'cracks by the eyes' + 'examining a forgery'
- M4 ultramarine pigment ← 'brushing sand from her dress' + 'too expensive, too pure, undiluted by turpentine'
- M5 reflection-only woman ← 'exists only as reflection of someone else's desire' + 'like a ghost'
Alternates from the other designs, if you prefer:
- M1: a blank cream auction lot tag tied to her scratched bangle (blank, because any number on it would be text that isn't yours).
- M2: pastel dust coming off her wrist onto his fingers ('collectors touch their Degas').
- M5: her reflection standing in heels in a campaign pose while she sits barefoot ('muscle memory of poses').

5. LOOKS YOUR TEXT DOES NOT GIVE (all my choices):
- Mila: her age (young), pale ash-blonde hair scraped back (chosen to contrast with Kira's black), and a BLACK knit dress at the landing. Your text only says the dress hugs her 'like a second breath'.
- Mila: the white silk-and-lace dress at dinner is from #083 (white, 'like a ghost'); the lace and the high-heeled sandals are mine.
- Jean-Marc: about fifty, dark hair silvering at the temples, clean-shaven, and the pale stone-grey suit, kept the same in every shot so the model holds him.
- Jean-Marc: the pale silk lining turns your 'voice like … silk lining' into clothing. 'A man who owes' is from #085 ('the one Jean owes').
- Kira at the jetty: a thin black strap only (not in your text). THAT dress is still first seen in 13.

6. TIME COMPRESSION AND ORDER. The poems give a night dinner (#083), a terrace (#084) and a copper sunset with Mila leaving (#085). I folded all of it into THAT-dress evening, because #086 joins the restaurant evening, the Jungle Dress, the necklace and the rain. The order is mine: sunset (M3) → first star (M4) → night (M5). Mila leaves BEFORE the empty-sofa frame. That inverts #083, where she is sitting barefoot at dinner.

7. A NEW COLOUR. Ultramarine (#083, 'a color Renoir probably never saw') is not in the scenario's colour chain. I placed it between copper and 15's storm night as your own instance of Law 5, 'a color that doesn't exist'. Keep or drop.

8. ULE IS NOT IN THE ARC. He is at the table off-frame, and Ule and Kira share no frame here; their next shared frame is 15. #082's handshake, where Jean-Marc appraises Ule 'like a canvas', is left out to avoid four faces in one frame. Optional extra shot if you want it: the handshake with a single fresh stroke of ultramarine oil paint hanging in the air between the two men ('The air between us thickens like oil paint on a palette before the first stroke', #082).

9. TWO TRICKS COULD FEEL REPEATED:
- M1's shadow rhymes with the shadowless red dog (17). If the dog's trick must stay unique, use the lot tag for M1.
- M5's glass trick sits beside k11's reflection that undresses. My reading: one woman with too much double, one who is only a double. If that is one glass too many, the alternative for M5 is the ultramarine night seeping through the window into the hem of her white dress, like dye climbing cloth.

10. OPTIONAL CONTINUITY. In M5, your necklace could lie on the table 'in a semicircle' (#086). That would imply Kira took it off herself before asking him to fasten it again in 16b. That is my reading of the arc, so it is not in the prompt.

11. CAPTIONS. M3's card names the detail it shows. If you want the cracks unexplained, the alternate card is 'examining a forgery — too perfect to be real.' (#085, verbatim clause). M4 and M5 use contiguous clauses of longer sentences, the way the scenario already uses 'asked him to fasten the Graff on her again.'

12. KEPT OUT ON PURPOSE:
- The phones (#082, #084): your no-stock-props rule.
- 'Dans l'Atuona qui se meurt…' (#083) and 'Il pleut des voix de femmes mortes d'amour…' (#084): they would be spoken, and not English.
- 'Jean freezes.' (#083): it would pre-empt 'Ule freezes.' (#098).
- Ule's 'four beats, pause' (#083): it breaks 'three notes, never four'.
- The debt / kept-woman plot, Gustav, Pastorales talk, 'Two billionaires', and Ule's notebook as a prop (it would clash with 21's notebook).
- Branded lines on screen (Saint Laurent, Alaïa, Sotheby's, Art Basel, Cartier, Hermès). You allowed 'Graff' and 'Comme des Garçons' on screen in v3, so a branded card is your call.

13. THE NAME. #083's English spells him 'Ole'. None of the chosen lines contains his name.

14. RUNTIME. +27 s takes the cut to about 4:57. Whether anything pays for it to hold 4:30 is your decision; I cut nothing.
